tagline: A technology leader in the digital transformation of industries
hero_kpi_rationale: The Electrification segment is a strategic pillar of ABB, driven by the energy transition and the growth of sustainable electrical infrastructure, particularly in smart cities and electric mobility.
company_description: ABB is a global leader in electrification, automation, and industrial digitalization technologies, providing solutions to enhance energy efficiency and productivity in infrastructure and industry.

kpis.name: Electrification Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by the division specializing in electrical solutions for buildings, infrastructure, and industries.
kpis.description: The Electrification segment has consistently contributed to ABB's revenue, supported by demand for energy efficiency and electric charging solutions.
kpis.signal: Key segment in the global energy transition.

kpis.name: Industrial Automation Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from automated systems for process and discrete industries.
kpis.description: The segment was affected in 2019 by declining demand, particularly in robotics, due to economic uncertainty.
kpis.signal: Impact of geopolitical tensions on industrial investments.

kpis.name: Motion Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue related to electric motors, variable speed drives, and drive systems.
kpis.description: The Motion segment remains resilient due to integration into critical industrial applications.
kpis.signal: Stability driven by motor energy efficiency.

kpis.name: Robotics Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from industrial robots and automation solutions for manufacturing.
kpis.description: The segment suffered from weak automation investments, particularly in Asia and Europe.
kpis.signal: Decline linked to low industrial confidence in 2019.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin reflects ABB's industrial efficiency and the value-added nature of its solutions.
kpis.signal: Solid margin for a technology-driven industrial company.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin has improved due to organizational simplification and efficiency gains.

kpis.name: R&D (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: ABB maintains a moderate level of R&D, focused on energy efficiency and digital platforms.
kpis.signal: Targeted investment in digital and energy innovation.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: Headcount has decreased following internal restructuring and refocusing on the four core businesses.
kpis.signal: Reduction as part of organizational simplification.

kpis.name: Orders
kpis.explanation: Measures the number of orders received by ABB, an indicator of future demand and commercial health.

kpis.name: Book-to-Bill
kpis.explanation: Ratio of orders received to sales realized; indicates whether future demand is increasing.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Measures the actual cash the company generates after investments, showing its ability to fund growth and dividends.

kpis.name: Electrification Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Measures the percentage of profit generated by ABB's Electrification division on its sales.

kpis.name: Motion Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Measures the profitability of ABB's Motion division: what percentage of sales turns into profit before taxes.

kpis.name: Dividend
kpis.explanation: The dividend measures the cash ABB distributes to its shareholders annually in return for their investment.

kpis.name: Net Cash
kpis.explanation: Measures available cash after debt repayment, indicating financial strength and investment capacity.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.94 CHF in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 1.907 Bn CHF in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 40.3% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Indicates the company's ability to generate profit per share: basis for calculating the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2020-2024). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Dependence on conflict minerals in the supply chain
risks.summary: ABB relies on 3TG minerals (gold, tantalum, tin, tungsten) sourced from high-risk areas, with 374 smelters/refineries identified in 2023. The company cannot guarantee the accuracy or completeness of supplier data, exposing ABB to regulatory non-compliance risks (SEC conflict minerals rule) and reputational damage.
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in detail in the CMR (Conflict Minerals Report), with moderate language but strict legal obligations (SEC Form SD). Trend is stable: 87% supplier response rate in 2023 vs 90% in 2022, indicating slight deterioration. Regulatory category carries high weight for an industrial company of this size.

risks.title: Opacity and limited traceability of multi-tier supply chain
risks.summary: ABB is structurally distant from smelters and refineries in its supply chain, making raw material traceability extremely difficult. In 2023, only 64% of identified smelters were RMAP-compliant, and suppliers often cannot confirm the use of specific smelters at the product level.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states that ABB is 'multiple levels upstream from smelters' and 'unable to exert direct influence', strong language indicating a structural vulnerability. Risk is recurring and stable, inherent to the complexity of ABB's global industrial supply chains.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of critical material suppliers in China
risks.summary: A significant portion of the smelters and refineries identified in ABB's supply chain are located in China (e.g., over 20 tantalum smelters, over 10 tungsten smelters). Disruptions due to trade tensions, sanctions, or Chinese export restrictions could impact ABB's global production.
risks.score_rationale: Annex I reveals a massive concentration of smelters in China for all four minerals (tantalum, tungsten, tin, gold), representing the majority of identified suppliers. In a context of rising geopolitical tensions, this risk is increasing. Geopolitical category has high impact for a global industrial group.

risks.title: Non-compliance of 36% of smelters with responsible sourcing standards RMAP
risks.summary: In 2023, 122 out of 374 identified smelters had not yet started the RMAP audit process, and ABB acknowledges it cannot determine the 'conflict' status of its entire supply chain. This exposes ABB to criticism from ESG investors and NGOs, as well as reputational risk if links to armed groups are established.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly states that 36% of identified smelters were not RMAP-compliant in 2023 (vs 35% in 2022), with language acknowledging the inability to determine conflict status for all. Reputational risk is stable but persistent, potentially worsening under ESG stakeholder pressure.

risks.title: Risk of SEC regulatory non-compliance on conflict minerals
risks.summary: ABB is subject to SEC reporting requirements on conflict minerals (Form SD, annual CMR) and cannot label its products as 'DRC conflict free'. Any changes in U.S. or European regulations (e.g., EU conflict minerals regulation) could increase due diligence obligations and compliance costs.
risks.score_rationale: ABB files a Form SD with the SEC and complies with the Dodd-Frank conflict minerals rule. The document explicitly notes that ABB has not concluded on the DRC status of its products, a delicate regulatory position. Risk is stable but under increasing regulatory scrutiny.

risks.title: Presence of Russian smelters in the supply chain under sanctions
risks.summary: Several Russian smelters and refineries appear in ABB's identified supply chain (notably for gold and tantalum), some potentially exposed to Western sanctions. ABB risks inadvertent sanctions violations, legal penalties, and reputational harm if these relationships are not promptly clarified and managed.
risks.score_rationale: Annex I lists several Russian smelters (gold, tantalum) including Solikamsk Magnesium Works, JSC Uralelectromed, OJSC Krastsvetmet, in a context of Western sanctions post-2022. Risk has sharply increased since the Ukraine invasion, with implicitly concerning language due to their mere presence on the list.

risks.title: Insufficient supplier engagement: 13% non-response rate to mineral surveys
risks.summary: In 2023, 13% of suppliers approached by ABB did not respond to conflict mineral surveys (vs 10% in 2022). This decline in engagement reduces ABB's visibility into its supply chain and weakens the quality of its regulatory reporting to the SEC.
risks.score_rationale: Supplier response rate declined from 90% in 2022 to 87% in 2023, signaling a negative trend. The document acknowledges 'challenges' for multi-tier suppliers. Moderate operational risk with slight deterioration, affecting regulatory reporting quality.

risks.title: Dependence on third parties (RMI/RMAP) for supplier validation
risks.summary: ABB fully delegates smelter validation to the RMI's RMAP program, without conducting direct audits. Any failure, loss of credibility, or change in RMI standards would expose ABB to gaps in its conflict minerals compliance program, with no immediate alternative available.
risks.score_rationale: ABB explicitly acknowledges reliance on RMI and the RMAP process to validate suppliers, without direct audit capability at smelters. This structural dependency on a third party is mentioned repeatedly. Risk is stable, inherent to ABB's operational model as a downstream consumer.
